Speculative decoding accelerates language model inference by leveraging a smaller, faster "draft" model to propose a sequence of future tokens, which are then verified in parallel by the larger, more accurate "target" model. Instead of generating tokens one by one, the target model evaluates the entire draft sequence simultaneously, significantly reducing the number of sequential steps required to produce output.

The process relies on a verification mechanism where the target model checks the draft tokens against its own probability distribution. If the draft tokens align with the target model’s predictions, they are accepted immediately; if a mismatch occurs, the target model corrects the error and generates the correct token from that point forward. This parallel verification allows the system to accept multiple tokens per step, provided the draft model is sufficiently aligned with the target model.

By minimizing the latency associated with autoregressive generation, speculative decoding achieves substantial speedups without compromising the quality or distribution of the final output. The technique is particularly effective when the draft model has a high acceptance rate, as it maximizes the number of tokens generated per computational step while maintaining the exact output probabilities of the original large model.
